speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific nature of the shooting pain, and does it occur when you touch the ear or move your jaw? Additionally, how long has it been since your tympanoplasty surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The shooting pain when eating suggests involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve, which is commonly injured during tympanoplasty; have you noticed any numbness or tingling on the side of your face as well? Also, does the pain radiate to your temple or cheek, and have you tried any pain medication that helps? REQUEST TEST: Audiogram and Tympanometry to assess current middle ear status.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-tympanoplasty Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (also known as Frey's syndrome or neuralgic otalgia).

I must clarify that tuberculosis is extremely unlikely given your history of recent ear surgery and the specific nature of pain triggered by chewing and jewelry; this clinical picture strongly points to nerve injury from the procedure. Please confirm if the pain also occurs when you eat sweet foods, as this would confirm Frey's syndrome.
